q-40882.name: Question 1
q-40882.problem: Consider the vector $u=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ \sqrt{k} \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Given that $u\cdot v=-20$ and $‖v‖=5$,  what is the smallest possible value of $k?$
q-40882.worked_solution:
We will use the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality,

$$
|u\cdot v|\le ‖u‖\cdot ‖v‖.
$$

We are given all the quantities in the inequality above, except for $‖u‖.$ So first, we compute $‖u‖$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖u‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(\sqrt{k})^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{14+k}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|u\cdot v| & \le ‖u‖\cdot ‖v‖ \\ |-20| & \le \sqrt{14+k}\cdot (5) \\ 4 & \le \sqrt{14+k} \\ {4}^{2} & \le {(\sqrt{14+k})}^{2} \\ 16 & \le 14+k \\ 2 & \le k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest possible value of $k$ is $2.$

q-74105.problem: Let $A(1,-3,2,-1)$ and $B(1,1,3,-2).$ Find the cosine of the angle $∠AOB$, where $O(0,0,0,0)$ is the origin.
q-74105.worked_solution:
First, let

$$
\begin{aligned}a=\overset{\to }{OA}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,b=\overset{\to }{OB}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Also, let $\theta =m∠AOB$ be the angle between the vectors $a$ and $b.$ Then, we can find $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{‖a‖\,‖b‖} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{1}{b}_{1}+{a}_{2}{b}_{2}+{a}_{3}{b}_{3}+{a}_{4}{b}_{4}}{\sqrt{{a}_{1}^{2}+{a}_{2}^{2}+{a}_{3}^{2}+{a}_{4}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{b}_{1}^{2}+{b}_{2}^{2}+{b}_{3}^{2}+{b}_{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot 1+2\cdot 3+(-1)\cdot (-2)}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}\,\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{15}\cdot \sqrt{15}} \\  & =\frac{6}{15} \\  & =\frac{6÷3}{15÷3} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

q-74127.problem: Let $A(4,-1,1,0)$, $B(4,2,1,-1)$, and $C(0,-5,3,2).$ Find the cosine of the angle $∠BAC.$
q-74127.worked_solution:
Let $v=\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $w=\overset{\to }{AC}.$ Then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =b-a \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}w & =c-a \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -4 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Let $\theta =m∠BAC$ be the angle between the vectors $v$ and $w.$ Then, we can find $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{v\cdot w}{‖v‖\,‖w‖} \\  & =\frac{{v}_{1}{w}_{1}+{v}_{2}{w}_{2}+{v}_{3}{w}_{3}+{v}_{4}{w}_{4}}{\sqrt{{v}_{1}^{2}+{v}_{2}^{2}+{v}_{3}^{2}+{v}_{4}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{w}_{1}^{2}+{w}_{2}^{2}+{w}_{3}^{2}+{w}_{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{0\cdot (-4)+3\cdot (-4)+0\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 2}{\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}\,\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-14}{\sqrt{10}\cdot \sqrt{40}} \\  & =-\frac{14}{20} \\  & =-\frac{14÷2}{20÷2} \\  & =-\frac{7}{10}\end{aligned}
$$

q-74110.problem: Let $A(0,-2,1,-3)$ and $B(-1,2,2,-3).$ Find the cosine of the angle $∠AOB$, where $O(0,0,0,0)$ is the origin.
q-74110.worked_solution:
First, let

$$
\begin{aligned}a=\overset{\to }{OA}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,b=\overset{\to }{OB}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Also, let $\theta =m∠AOB$ be the angle between the vectors $a$ and $b.$ Then, we can find $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{‖a‖\,‖b‖} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{1}{b}_{1}+{a}_{2}{b}_{2}+{a}_{3}{b}_{3}+{a}_{4}{b}_{4}}{\sqrt{{a}_{1}^{2}+{a}_{2}^{2}+{a}_{3}^{2}+{a}_{4}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{b}_{1}^{2}+{b}_{2}^{2}+{b}_{3}^{2}+{b}_{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{0\cdot (-1)+(-2)\cdot 2+1\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot (-3)}{\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}}\,\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-3)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{7}{\sqrt{14}\cdot \sqrt{18}} \\  & =\frac{7}{\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{7}\cdot 3\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{7}}{6}\end{aligned}
$$
